title: Homogeneous polynomials with nonzero vertex image become monic in a linear direction
statement: Let $k$ be an infinite field and let $B$ be a standard graded $k$-algebra, so $B=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}B_j$, $B_0=k$, and $B_+=\bigoplus_{j>0}B_j$ [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. Give $P=B[T_1,\ldots,T_e]$ the total grading with $\deg T_i=1$, where $e\ge1$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $n\ge1$ and let $f\in P_n$ be homogeneous. Let $\epsilon:P\to k[T_1,\ldots,T_e]$ be coefficientwise reduction modulo $B_+$ and suppose $H=\epsilon(f)\ne0$. There exist $v\in k^e\setminus\{0\}$ with $H(v)\ne0$ and $M\in\operatorname{GL}_e(k)$ with first column $v$ such that the graded $B$-algebra automorphism $\sigma_M$, defined by $T_i\mapsto\sum_jM_{ij}T_j$, makes $\sigma_M(f)$ a degree-$n$ polynomial in $T_1$ over $D=B[T_2,\ldots,T_e]$ whose leading coefficient is the nonzero scalar $H(v)$. In particular $H(v)^{-1}\sigma_M(f)$ is monic in $D[T_1]$, and multiplication by $f$ on $P$ is injective.

proof.text: Expand $f=\sum_\alpha b_\alpha T^\alpha$, where $|\alpha|=\sum_i\alpha_i$. By the total grading and [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra], each nonzero $b_\alpha$ lies in $B_{n-|\alpha|}$, and $|\alpha|\le n$. Reduction modulo $B_+$ kills the terms with $|\alpha|<n$ and is the identity on $B_0=k$. Hence $H=\sum_{|\alpha|=n}b_\alpha T^\alpha$ is a nonzero homogeneous form of degree $n$ over $k$. In particular the $T$-degree-$n$ part of $f$ has scalar coefficients.

proof.text: List the indices other than $r$ as $i_2,\ldots,i_e$. Let $M$ have columns $v,e_{i_2},\ldots,e_{i_e}$, where $e_i$ is the coordinate vector. For $y=Mx$ its inverse is explicitly $x_1=v_r^{-1}y_r$ and $x_j=y_{i_j}-v_{i_j}v_r^{-1}y_r$ for $j\ge2$; substitution verifies both inverse identities. Thus $M\in\operatorname{GL}_e(k)$ and its first column is $v$. By the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], substitution $T_i\mapsto\sum_jM_{ij}T_j$ defines a $B$-algebra map $\sigma_M$. Substitution for $M^{-1}$ is its inverse: on $T_i$ their composites have coefficient matrices $MM^{-1}$ and $M^{-1}M$. Each image of a variable is homogeneous of degree one and coefficients in $B$ are fixed, so both maps preserve the total grading.

proof.text: Group monomials by their exponent of $T_1$ to identify $P$ with $D[T_1]$, $D=B[T_2,\ldots,T_e]$: $bT_1^{a_1}\cdots T_e^{a_e}$ corresponds to $(bT_2^{a_2}\cdots T_e^{a_e})T_1^{a_1}$; the inverse expands its coefficients. These maps preserve products because exponents add. Each substituted monomial from step 1 has $T_1$-degree at most $|\alpha|\le n$. It contributes to the coefficient of $T_1^n$ only if $|\alpha|=n$, and then only by choosing $M_{i1}T_1=v_iT_1$ from every factor. The coefficient is therefore $\sum_{|\alpha|=n}b_\alpha\prod_i v_i^{\alpha_i}=H(v)=c$. This is a nonzero scalar in $B_0=k\subset D$, so $\sigma_M(f)$ has $T_1$-degree exactly $n$ and $q:=c^{-1}\sigma_M(f)$ is monic.

proof.text: The ring $D$ is commutative, so apply [lem-weil-pbc-monic-polynomial-nonzerodivisor] to the monic polynomial $q\in D[T_1]$. If $fg=0$ in $P$, applying $\sigma_M$ and multiplying by the scalar $c^{-1}$ gives $q\sigma_M(g)=0$. The cited statement gives $\sigma_M(g)=0$, and applying the explicit inverse substitution gives $g=0$. Finally $fg=fh$ implies $f(g-h)=0$ and hence $g=h$, proving injectivity of multiplication by $f$.
